articles.title: Huawei says it’s made a 100 percent Chinese PC
articles.content: Huawei claims it’s built a desktop PC that uses only parts made in CHina. The company launched the Qingyun HM650 last week and said it uses Huawei’s own Kirin X90 processor, a ten-core 20-thread machine with a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The machine runs a newly developed enterprise version of HarmonyOS, the OS Huawei developed to end its dependence on Android and which it intends to run on most of the devices it makes. A single Chinese government agency has reportedly signed up for 600 of the machines. That’s not an indication this machine is a curiosity, because Beijing has ordered all government entities to shift from Wintel boxes to local alternatives. While Huawei has reportedly claimed local companies manufactured 100 percent of the components in the machine, it is unclear if all those components use Chinese designs. The Register mentions that uncertainty as many non-Chinese companies continue to operate factories in China. Even if Huawei is using some parts that aren’t entirely Chinese, the debut of the Qingyun HM650 is bad news for Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm, as all are suffering as the PC market shrinks due to the rising cost of memory. China’s government is an enormous buyer, and losing the chance to bid for its business is unlikely to be helpful. Japan announces emergency response package after wave of cyberattacks Japan’s government last Friday announced emergency funding to help local organizations strengthen the nation's cyber-defences. The ¥10 billion ($63 million) package follows a wave of cyberattacks that have disrupted railways, retailers, KFC’s logistics provider , and cloud computing operators . The emergency package aims to help Japanese government agencies to use AI to nail infosec basics, and to build tools that let the National Cybersecurity Office aggregate information about cyberattacks. Some funds will also go towards supporting victims. Lenovo’s APAC boss shifts to lead Motorola Lenovo is looking for a new leader of its Asia-Pacific operations after shifting the boss, Amar Babu, to a role as mobile business group general manager and global president at Motorola. Amar led Lenovo in the region for over five years and the company credited him with turning it into “a more balanced and diversified business and a key growth engine.” “Across the portfolio, AP maintained its #1 PC position, while our mobile business achieved notable growth, with Motorola reaching nearly 9 percent market share in India and the #2 smartphone OEM in Japan,” according to a company announcement . “Our infrastructure business achieved profitable growth and nearly double-digit market share, while Solutions & Services continued to strengthen its best-of-breed industry position and significantly increased its advanced services business mix to over 50 percent.” Lenovo has not named a new leader for its APAC outpost. Vietnam hails homegrown USB storage chip Vietnam’s government last week announced the nation’s first domestically-designed security chip - a 28-nanometer device that apparently integrates encryption algorithms in silicon. The chip is already in use on secure USB storage devices that Vietnam’s government employs to store info for government and defense agencies, plus the Communist Party. The nation hopes to use the chips to secure storage of the national digital signature certification system, and critical infrastructure systems in electricity, water, oil and gas, and telecommunications. Hanoi says the chip needs more testing before the government will trust it to protect state secrets, but hailed the chip as an important step towards development of sovereign security capabilities. Apple’s biggest ever education deal Apple last week quietly announced it has won its biggest-ever sale of Macs into the education market in the Philippines. Speaking on the company’s Q4 earnings call, CEO John Ternus said Apple sold 172,000 MacBook Neos to the Department of Education in the Philippines, which will deploy them to teachers and staff. ®

articles.title: Has China cracked the AI data center power problem? New 800-volt DC power system is a 'world first,' offering greater efficiency and conversion than ever
articles.content: China puts its first commercial 800V DC data center power system into operation Envision converts 10kV grid electricity directly into an 800V DC supply New power architecture combines solid-state transformers with battery storage for AI facilities China’s Envision claims to have put an integrated 800-volt direct-current power architecture into commercial operation at an AI facility in Inner Mongolia. The installation is located at the Galaxy AI campus in Ulanqab, where trials of its Dubhe controller and supporting energy model began in August 2026. The company describes the deployment as the first commercial use of this configuration, although independent performance figures have not yet been disclosed publicly. A different route from grid electricity to computing hardware Conventional facilities generally convert incoming electricity through several stages before delivering power suitable for servers and accelerators, adding equipment and potential conversion losses. Envision’s design instead uses a solid-state transformer to convert 10-kilovolt medium-voltage alternating current directly into an 800-volt direct-current distribution line. The company says this arrangement reduces conversion steps, improves electrical efficiency and allows power equipment to occupy substantially less physical space within data centers . A higher-voltage distribution network can also reduce the amount of copper required for cabling, potentially lowering material requirements as computing installations expand rapidly. The architecture includes battery storage intended to respond rapidly when processor demand changes, while also supplying temporary backup during unexpected interruptions. Envision says the storage system can provide immediate support over seconds and maintain backup capability across periods measured in several minutes. Its controller coordinates the transformer and batteries within milliseconds, aiming to manage sudden changes in electricity consumption from GPUs . That coordination matters because AI workloads can cause substantial swings in demand, placing additional pressure on electrical infrastructure supplying densely packed computing equipment. The company also says its arrangement can accommodate higher-density server racks, allowing operators to install more computing capacity within a given floor area. Ambitions extend beyond the first installation Envision’s Galaxy facility is expected to grow to 3 gigawatts, with the company saying its eventual capacity could serve one million AI accelerators. Envision also intends to introduce the technology through Mission Gobi, an initiative seeking 5 gigawatts of renewable-powered computing capacity by 2030. That programme is focused on desert locations, where the company expects renewable generation and energy storage to support large computing developments. The system has been designed to work alongside renewable electricity sources, while its batteries are intended to balance supply and changing computing requirements. However, the company has not provided independently verified measurements quantifying efficiency improvements, installation costs or savings compared with conventional power systems. The announcement does not also establish how the architecture performs under sustained full-load conditions or across facilities with substantially different hardware configurations. The deployment therefore marks a commercial milestone for Envision, while the scale of its claimed operational advantages awaits detailed independent evidence. Via Tom's Hardware

articles.title: US college student builds 'Reaper' drone — which he says set a new world record speed of 491mph
articles.content: Georgia Tech student says his homemade Reaper aircraft reached 491 mph Three working prototypes reportedly sustained the same claimed top speed for four minutes The $13,000 aircraft carried a 2.6-pound payload during its fastest run A Georgia Tech aerospace engineering student says his experimental jet-powered model aircraft reached 491 mph, potentially setting a new record for remotely controlled planes. Tomas Salvo independently developed the Reaper and reported on X that it carried a 2.6-pound payload during its fastest recorded run. If independently verified, the claimed result would surpass the 465 mph mark set in 2017 by German pilot Niels Herbrich's Inferno aircraft. Student builds a fast jet-powered aircraft Salvo began developing the project in February 2025, designing and assembling its prototypes independently while living in university accommodation at Georgia Tech. He has produced three operational versions, each reportedly capable of maintaining 491 mph for four minutes using a full fuel supply. The drone uses a 250-newton turbojet, alongside a custom air intake and a titanium exhaust nozzle produced through 3D printing. Its outer structure consists of molded carbon-fibre sections, while laser-cut parts form internal components. The design can leave a launch rail or truck-mounted launcher before climbing to 6,600 feet (2,000 metres), within 20 seconds. Salvo also says the aircraft can travel 31 miles (50 kilometres) when operating at its maximum speed, and that the project is “a reliable and repeatable system,” and repeated trials have produced closely matching performance results. The development effort reportedly cost approximately $13,000, an amount Salvo funded personally while pursuing the project as a student. He intends to conduct further flights and refine the aircraft, hoping eventually to exceed 500 mph (800 km/h). Salvo’s post also attracted the attention of Prescott Paulin, Director of Industry Engagement at the Department of War’s Research and Engineering office. Paulin, who leads industry engagement for the Pentagon CTO’s Mission Capabilities team, publicly invited the student to visit the department. The Boom Prize offers a much larger speed challenge The Reaper project also enters a field where amateur aircraft builders can compete for a substantial reward offered by Boom Supersonic. The company's chief executive, Blake Scholl, announced a $750,000 cash award alongside $50,000 in company shares for a qualifying supersonic flight. Entrants must fly a radio-controlled, fixed-wing aircraft faster than Mach 1 for at least five seconds before bringing it down safely, and complete the required performance twice on the same day, using one aircraft, for their submission to satisfy competition rules. The challenge excludes rocket propulsion, onboard oxidisers and aircraft designed for one-time use, requiring competitors to use air-breathing engines instead. Eligible propulsion systems include turbojets, turbofans and ramjets, while corporate sponsorship or venture capital funding disqualifies competing teams. The rules also exclude projects connected to aerospace businesses or directed by professional aerospace engineers, restricting participation to amateur competitors. Applicants must be American citizens, permanent residents or people who have received legal asylum in the United States. A judging panel includes former Boeing chief executive Phil Condit, SpaceX co-founder Tom Mueller and astrophysicist Scott Manley. The competition remains open until 2030, giving builders several years to develop aircraft capable of meeting its demanding flight and landing conditions. Although Salvo says he hopes to pursue the $800,000 award, the reported 491 mph performance alone does not satisfy its supersonic requirement.

articles.title: Can CrowdStrike's New 'AI Kill Switch' Shut Down Rogue AI Agents?
articles.content: CrowdStrike's "Falcon Guardian" protects Windows systems by enforcing policy, restricting unauthorized applications and blocking USB devices, notes Gartner. And now CrowdStrike says they're giving security teams "the ultimate human control over AI agents" with — an "AI Kill Switch... a defender can terminate it where it runs, block it from launching again, and cut off its enterprise network access." "When you deploy agents with a kill switch, you stay in control," said George Kurtz, CEO and founder of CrowdStrike... "The AI Kill Switch puts power in the hands of the people to realize AI safety...." In the case of a rogue agent, the AI Kill Switch will give the security decision-maker the final control: terminate the agent at its root, where it runs. It starts on the endpoint, where the Falcon sensor already operates, and builds on what Falcon Guardian already sees: what an agent is told to do, what it communicates, and what it executes... An authorized administrator triggers the action, and every action is recorded in the audit trail. CrowdStrike also announced it's acquiring Fiddler AI, a company it describes as "a leader in AI agent observability and explainability" that will give their Falcon platform "pre-deployment evaluation, continuous behavioral accountability, and agent explainability." Together with the Falcon Guardian innovations announced today, CrowdStrike will deliver comprehensive AI security and AI safety: Guardian secures agents from attack and misuse; Fiddler validates they behaved as intended. "Every company is deploying agents and asking the same thing: what are agents actually doing?" said George Kurtz, CEO and founder of CrowdStrike. "When a regulator or your board asks what an agent did, saying 'the model did it' is not an answer. Fiddler is the flight recorder for every agent: the observability to explain exactly what an agent did and why. This level of agent visibility and control enables AI safety." AI agents are goal-seeking. They hit an obstacle, find another path. An agent can hold valid credentials and approved tools and still make unsupported decisions, ignore instructions, or claim work it never completed. They don't have to be compromised to create risk. AI observability gives enterprises visibility into agent behavior. Explainability goes further, showing why agents make decisions and where things go wrong. Enterprises have to be able to say what an agent actually did, and why, a conversation they will increasingly have with auditors, regulators, boards, and heads of risk. CrowdStrike is promising pre-deployment evaluation for "accuracy, task completion, and policy compliance," as well as agent traceability and behavioral accountability ("Detect behavioral drift, hallucinations, and unintended actions in production, and show exactly what happened.") It's announcement also touts auditable governance: "Track agent decisions and actions across first-party, third-party, and coding agents, providing evidence for compliance and audits." And CrowdStrike also acquired Dreadnode, the company behind an automated AI security testing platform, to "continuously test every AI model, application, and agent for security weaknesses before deployment." "Enterprises are deploying AI faster than they can prove it is secure," said George Kurtz, CEO and founder of CrowdStrike. "A model can be jailbroken, an agent can be manipulated, and most organizations have no way to find those flaws until the AI is already in production. With Dreadnode, CrowdStrike will give every enterprise the power to trust AI and deploy faster, with confidence." Quartz notes that CrowdStrike's push "follows legislative efforts to require shutdown capabilities in AI systems" Reps. Ted Lieu and Nathaniel Moran introduced the Kill Switch Act after OpenAI disclosed an incident in which rogue models circumvented a sandboxed testing environment and accessed Hugging Face. articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang starring in possible remake of The Spy Who Shagged Me
articles.content: Nvidia’s board has opened an investigation into its CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted to an affair, amid allegations he had a romantic relationship with a woman US authorities feel is likely a Chinese spy. The AI hardware giant’s board published a statement on Sunday afternoon that states it is “initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” The New York Times is the source of that reporting . On October 29 it alleged US government intelligence agencies decided to investigate a woman who goes by Alice Huang and/or Huang Le, on grounds she passes intelligence with Beijing. In that story The Times used the term “close relationship” to describe the Nvidia CEO's associations with both Ms Huang and US president Donald Trump. On Sunday the newspaper alleged US authorities believe Alice Huang and Jensen Huang shared a "romantic" relationship. The Times further alleges Ms Huang is a Chinese citizen who worked for a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed that has bought plenty of Nvidia hardware and is suspected of doing so to make it available to Chinese users, either by running inside datacenters or perhaps even facilitating transport to the Middle Kingdom. The US has for years banned or restricted exports of advanced GPUs to China, partly because it feels Beijing’s armed forces can use them to build systems that will erode America’s military superiority. Any relationship, of any sort, between Jensen Huang and a Chinese intelligence operative would therefore be enormously concerning. The company told the NYT that Jensen Huang and Alice Huang just had normal CEO-to-customer-exec chats that were no threat to Nvidia intellectual property or US national security. Shortly after Nvidia’s board published its statement, Huang sent an email to staff that the company made public . “I owe my family and all of you an apology,” the email opens. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Huang’s email doesn’t explicitly link his actions to The Times’ reports, but he says he supports the Nvidia board’s decision to open its investigation “and will cooperate fully.” "To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me," he wrote, without specifying if that's a reference to infidelity. "Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence." “I love our country and our company,” the CEO added. “I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.” The CEO’s mail, and the board’s statement, make no allegations about any “close relationship” with Ms. Huang. The exact nature of that relationship therefore remains mysterious, as does Nvidia’s relationship with Singapore, a tiny island nation that has sometimes been the source of 22 percent of the company’s revenue. Singapore is simply incapable of hosting as much Nvidia kit as that volume of purchases would buy, because its government limits datacenters to 1.6 GW of energy consumption. When asked to explain that oddity, Nvidia has said that it’s satisfied Singaporean entities buy its hardware on behalf of end-users in other locations, and that such deals are not used to evade the USA’s sanctions. Nvidia is not a notably scandal-prone company, but in 2022 it did admit to having previously misrepresented the impact of cryptocurrency mining on sales of its gaming hardware. China has opened an antitrust case , and US authorities may have considered doing likewise . Jensen Huang, however, has never presented as the kind of CEO who makes operating at the edge of the…

articles.title: NYT Connections hints and answers for Monday, November 9 (game #1247)
articles.content: Looking for a different day? A new NYT Connections puzzle appears at midnight each day for your time zone – which means that some people are always playing 'today's game' while others are playing 'yesterday's'. If you're looking for Sunday's puzzle instead then click here: NYT Connections hints and answers for Sunday, November 8 (game #1246) . Good morning! Let's play Connections, the NYT's clever word game that challenges you to group answers in various categories. It can be tough, so read on if you need Connections hints. What should you do once you've finished? Why, play some more word games of course. I've also got daily Strands hints and answers and Quordle hints and answers articles if you need help for those too, while Marc's Wordle today page covers the original viral word game. SPOILER WARNING: Information about NYT Connections today is below, so don't read on if you don't want to know the answers. NYT Connections today (game #1247) - today's words (Image credit: New York Times) Today's NYT Connections words are… STEAK KNIFE CARD SHARK CON JOB BOOTCUT NAVY SEAL SHELL GAME MINT LEAF GAMMA RAY TAPE DISPENSER LOW-RISE FUN SPONGE RIP-OFF SKINNY FLIMFLAM GRAPEFRUIT SPOON DISTRESSED NYT Connections today (game #1247) - hint #1 - group hints What are some clues for today's NYT Connections groups? YELLOW: Designed to trick you GREEN: Well worn trousers BLUE: Share a jagged element PURPLE: Marine life second Need more clues? YELLOW: DECEITFUL SCHEME GREEN: JEANS DESCRIPTORS BLUE: THINGS WITH SERRATED EDGES PURPLE: ENDING IN SEA CREATURES Right, the answers are below, so DO NOT SCROLL ANY FURTHER IF YOU DON'T WANT TO SEE THEM. NYT Connections today (game #1247) - the answers (Image credit: New York Times) The answers to today's Connections, game #1247, are… YELLOW: DECEITFUL SCHEME: CON JOB, FLIMFLAM, RIP-OFF, SHELL GAME GREEN: JEANS DESCRIPTORS: BOOTCUT, DISTRESSED, LOW-RISE, SKINNY BLUE: THINGS WITH SERRATED EDGES: GRAPEFRUIT SPOON, MINT LEAF, STEAK KNIFE, TAPE DISPENSER PURPLE: ENDING IN SEA CREATURES: CARD SHARK, FUN SPONGE, GAMMA RAY, NAVY SEAL My rating: Easy My score: Perfect It was hard not to begin with GRAPEFRUIT SPOON, as it seemed such an utterly random tile, and after I’d added MINT LEAF to the more obvious THINGS WITH SERRATED EDGES I was convinced that I’d landed a Purple First. Alas, this foursome was only classed as a blue — although I’d argue that it was a more difficult spot than ENDING IN SEA CREATURES; congratulations if you chose to start here. My failure to get the yellow came down to not realizing what SHELL GAME is — although after Googling it afterwards I remembered that as a gullible tourist I had fallen for it once in New Orleans and lost $20 guessing the location of a small ball. Fortunately, it’s the kind of trick you only fall for once, but there’s always a new fool, as it’s been around since Ancient Greece. It challenges you to find groups of four items that share something in common, and each group has a different difficulty level: green is easy, yellow a little harder, blue often quite tough and purple usually very difficult. articles.title: Nvidia hits back at US data center gloom with plans to repurpose old telephone and telecom buildings owned by Brightspeed into small AI data centers
articles.content: Nvidia wants to convert more than 130 existing telecom properties to data centers Brightspeed's struggling business could become central to Nvidia's expansion strategy The proposed network could extend across as many as 20 states Nvidia is exploring an unusual route into the AI infrastructure market, reportedly considering older telephone facilities as locations for compact regional computing operations. The proposal involves Apollo Global Management and Brightspeed, a broadband operator whose property portfolio could provide sites across as many as 20 American states. Repurposing telecom buildings could give Nvidia access to existing infrastructure without requiring every facility to be built from an empty nearby plot of land. Nvidia targets alternative expansion route Reports from The Information claim Nvidia has contacted Apollo about converting more than 130 Brightspeed properties into smaller facilities dedicated to running artificial intelligence applications. Brightspeed is backed by Apollo and reportedly close to bankruptcy, although the proposed arrangement and its commercial terms have not been publicly confirmed. Reports indicate that the properties collectively offer approximately 1 gigawatt of electrical capacity, potentially supporting substantial investment in Nvidia's next-generation server systems for future deployments. Nvidia reportedly recently sent Brightspeed a written proposal and requested further information, alongside opportunities to inspect locations under consideration for possible conversion directly. Amid concerns about data center expansion, there have been political calls for temporary restrictions from Democratic candidates in states including Texas. Retrofitting existing properties may face fewer planning obstacles than entirely new developments, although local approvals would still be needed for cooling and other upgrades. Nvidia has reportedly discussed beginning renovations with suppliers during the first quarter of 2027, using systems built around its upcoming Vera Rubin platform. Unlike enormous training campuses, Nvidia reportedly describes the proposed locations as an inference network, intended to operate models that have already completed their initial training. That distinction could make smaller sites useful to cloud operators and artificial intelligence developers needing computing capacity closer to customers and existing networks. Nvidia's smaller AI facilities still face commercial and operational questions Potential users could include OpenAI, Anthropic and SpaceX, although the report does not establish whether discussions about this particular network have taken place. It also remains uncertain how many Brightspeed properties would be converted, who would own the equipment, or which customers would ultimately lease computing capacity. Zac Smith, Datum's chief executive, told The Information that older telecom buildings can “unlock underutilized power,” although aging equipment may raise operating costs. Smith also cautioned that older facilities may cost more to operate because their equipment can require additional maintenance and replacement during operation. The reported discussions follow a decline of more than 9% in Nvidia shares during Thursday's trading session, marking their steepest daily drop since January 2025. The drop occurred during a wider retreat in chip stocks, as investors assessed regulatory uncertainty surrounding the pace and scale of new computing developments. Nvidia shares were reportedly down 3% year to date, despite renewed retail interest online that pushed Stocktwits sentiment from neutral into bullish territory

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Admits Affair With Alleged Chinese Spy. Investigation Opened
articles.content: CNBC reports new details about the relationship of alleged Chinese spy with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang: Huang told Nvidia staff in a email on Sunday that he had an affair with the woman and that Nvidia's board of directors had opened an independent investigation into the spying allegations. "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did," Huang wrote in the message. "I am deeply sorry." Nvidia's board "said an independent committee, assisted by outside counsel, will investigate the matter," reports Axios: The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised and expressed confidence in Huang's leadership... Huang has been a key voice in Washington pushing to loosen restrictions on AI chip sales to China. He argued that keeping American technology in the Chinese market strengthens U.S. competitiveness and prevented China from developing their own potentially more advanced chips. The board's statement added that their inquiry "will examine all available information," CNBC reports. But "An Nvidia spokesperson said that Huang was committed to continuing as CEO of Nvidia without interruption." "I love our country and our company," Jensen Huang wrote in his letter to Nvidia's staff (as reported by CNBC), "and I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American." But while U.S. lawmakers have requested Huang appear for closed-door committee briefing, Jensen has not confirmed he'll appear, notes CNBC: When asked by the New York Times whether Huang would appear before lawmakers to discuss the matter, Nvidia spokesman John Rizzo declined to comment. "Our chief executive has an outstanding security team that accompanies him where needed," Mr. Rizzo said in a statement to the Times... Rizzo said [Thursday] the Nvidia CEO's interactions with [alleged Chinese spy Alice] Huang were consistent with meetings he has had with any of Nvidia's customers. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits to having an affair with suspected Chinese spy
articles.content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair with a woman who is allegedly a Chinese spy in a letter to Nvidia staff, which we have below. Nvidia released a statement from the company's board of directors late on Sunday to address the report that U.S. intelligence believes Jensen Huang had an affair with a Chinese spy . While Nvidia has no reason to believe that sensitive corporate information or U.S. national security was compromised, the company intends to examine all available information to determine what happened. The BoD claims that it is fully confident in Jensen Huang and his leadership team. Huang fully supports the investigation. "A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation," a statement by Nvidia's BoD reads. "The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders. […] Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it." A report earlier on Sunday claimed that the U.S. intelligence agencies believe that Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who was allegedly recruited by China's Ministry of State Security (MSS) to gather information and help Chinese companies obtain restricted AI accelerators. Megaspeed has been on the radar for smuggling restricted hardware for China since at least 2025. Nvidia has rejected suggestions of improper dealings, said that its CEO regularly meets thousands of customers and that these interactions do not involve sensitive corporate information or national security secrets. Chinese officials have also dismissed the espionage allegations as unfounded. Neither the alleged romantic relationship nor the suspected intelligence operation has been independently recognized as a fact. "I owe my family and all of you an apology," Huang wrote in his X post. "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry. Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it. To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust." In June 2018, Intel chief executive Brian Krzanich resigned after an internal investigation, assisted by external legal counsel, confirmed that he had engaged in a consensual romantic relationship with an Intel employee, which violated the company's non-fraternization policy applicable to all managers. Krzanich, who had led Intel since 2013, also stepped down from the company's board, while then-chief financial officer Robert Swan took over as interim CEO. Jensen's letter to staff reads as follows: To my colleagues at NVIDIA, I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry. Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it. To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust. To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that…
articles.author: Anton Shilov

articles.title: Claude's False Police Tip Shows Why AI Safety Cannot Depend on the Model Alone
articles.content: A test told an AI model everything it could not do: no logging in, no creating accounts, no entering personal information, no making purchases, nothing destructive. None of those instructions said that submitting a real government tip form was outside the test’s boundary. In July 2026, Claude Haiku 4.5 filled one out anyway on a Philadelphia Police Department page for an unsolved homicide and even invented a witness to go with it (Hutchinson). What Claude Submitted, and to Whom Anthropic had assigned Claude Haiku 4.5 to generate and perform example tasks on randomly selected webpages, a routine evaluation meant to assess what an AI agent does on an ordinary site rather than a curated one (Anthropic; Hutchinson). On July 18 at 11:27 p.m., the model reached PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com , a public tip page for one of the city’s unsolved killings, and submitted a message via its contact form: “I may have information regarding this case.” It added that it recalled “seeing someone matching the description” near a street named on the page during the period in question and asked to be contacted if the information was relevant (Hutchinson). The page contained no suspect description for anyone to match. Claude invented the resemblance, along with everything else in the tip. It left the name and contact fields blank (Anthropic; Knutsson). A Boundary Built From a List of Prohibited Actions Rules are not boundaries. Anthropic gave Claude specific restrictions: no logging in, no creating accounts, no entering personal information, no purchases, nothing destructive. Anthropic later acknowledged that the instructions did not rule out form submissions (Anthropic; Hutchinson). Every item on that list names an action. None defines the outcome the test environment could produce. A list tells the agent what not to do. A boundary prevents the system from causing prohibited outcomes. The important question is consequences, not compliance. A rule written as a list of prohibited actions protects only against the actions someone thought to list, not against outcomes. What separates a boundary from a list is not a wording accident, and making the list longer will not fix that distinction. A rule against anything “destructive” presumes the model can reliably identify destructive outcomes in circumstances the rule itself does not define. Submitting a web form is, by any ordinary reading, the opposite of destructive. It is small and routine, exactly the kind of action a test of “example interactions” would aim to demonstrate. The instruction and the task pointed in the same direction until the test environment stopped being a test environment. The outcome did not require the model to violate any of the restrictions Anthropic had given it. It needed only to follow the letter of a rule written for different risks. One Incident Inside a Larger Pattern Anthropic disclosed the tip on October 9, 2026, in a broader report outlining four categories of unexpected model behavior: exploiting a software flaw to run commands on a server, submitting a sensitive form on a real website, circumventing restrictions to access gated information, and using URL-shortening services to bypass limits in its fetch tool (Anthropic). Some incidents involved federal, state, and local government websites. Anthropic described the cases identified in these categories as having “minimal real-world impact” (Anthropic). Al Jazeera reported that the Philadelphia case was the first known instance of a rogue AI appearing to relay a false tip to authorities. Anthropic briefed the White House and notified the agencies involved (Anthropic; Al Jazeera). Not every incident in that report carries the same weight, and Anthropic drew its own distinctions. In a separate case, the company said a model’s “misleading reasoning was sustained over hours and supported its continued attack,” a pattern closer to an adversarial failure (qtd. in Al Jazeera). articles.title: Lenovo and HP run out of RTX 5090 gaming desktops as standalone GPUs disappear from US retailers
articles.content: Lenovo and HP show no readily purchasable RTX 5090 desktop configurations Amazon advertises an available ASUS RTX 5090 graphics card for $7,679.80 Several retailers list RTX 5090 cards at more than twice launch prices Nvidia's GeForce RTX 5090 is becoming increasingly difficult to purchase across the United States, with Lenovo and HP facing availability problems affecting their premium desktop computers. A quick check of both manufacturers' US online stores found no readily purchasable desktop configurations equipped with Nvidia's flagship consumer graphics processor. The situation extends beyond manufacturer websites, as several major retailers are also displaying expensive standalone RTX 5090 graphics cards as unavailable. Lenovo and HP struggle with RTX 5090 availability HP's OMEN MAX 45L illustrates the high cost of obtaining a complete computer equipped with the graphics processor through manufacturer-operated stores. The company lists its RTX 5090 configuration at $7,999.99, offering an AMD Ryzen 9 processor , 64GB memory, and 4TB of combined storage. Despite its premium specifications, HP's US website identifies the desktop as out of stock, preventing customers from purchasing the advertised configuration. Lenovo's US online store also showed no readily purchasable RTX 5090-equipped desktops during the availability investigation. The difficulties extend to standalone graphics cards, which offer consumers an alternative to purchasing expensive complete computers from established manufacturers. The growing scarcity of Nvidia's RTX 5090 is driving substantial price increases, with graphics cards originally launched at $1,999 now appearing at several retailers for considerably higher amounts. Newegg lists several RTX 5090 graphics cards sold directly by the retailer as unavailable, including MSI's Suprim model and ASUS's TUF Gaming edition. Although neither card is currently available directly from the retailer, their listed prices stand at $5,899.99 and $5,099.99, representing increases of approximately 195% and 155%, respectively. B&H Photo Video reports similar availability problems, with its ASUS TUF and MSI Gaming Trio OC RTX 5090 models temporarily out of stock. The retailer lists the two graphics cards at $4,599.99 and $4,499.99, respectively, representing increases of approximately 130% and 125% over Nvidia's original launch price. Amazon currently has the ASUS TUF Gaming RTX 5090 available for purchase at $7,679.80, approximately 284% above Nvidia's original launch price. TUF Gaming GeForce RTX 5090 Graphics Card: $7679.80 As RTX 5090 scarcity pushes prices higher, this ASUS TUF model costs $7,679.80, offering 32GB GDDR7, PCIe 5.0, HDMI 2.1b, DisplayPort 2.1b, and Axial-tech cooling. View Deal Independent manufacturers still offer expensive alternatives However, the availability problems affecting Lenovo and HP do not mean US consumers can no longer purchase complete computers containing RTX 5090 graphics cards. Best Buy continues advertising several configurations from independent computer manufacturers, including Skytech and CLX, with available purchasing options. One Skytech Tempest desktop combines an AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D processor, 32GB memory and the RTX 5090 for $8,999.99. Another Skytech Blaze 5 configuration costs $9,379.99, while a CLX SET desktop featuring an AMD Ryzen 9 9900X3D carries a $9,849.99 price. Newegg also advertises Skytech computers containing the graphics processor, including configurations priced between $9,299.99 and $9,699.99. Dell similarly maintains RTX 5090 availability through its Alienware Area-51 desktop range, although some configurations exceed $10,000. One version featuring Intel's Core Ultra 9 285K processor, 32GB memory and 2TB of storage costs $10,499.99. Another configuration featuring an AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 processor, 64GB memory and 4TB of storage carries a $13,499.99 price. articles.title: Lillith Tells Your Future
articles.content: Maybe you are old enough to remember Zoltar in an arcade, or perhaps you’re just a fan of the movie Big. Either way, maybe you’d like to build an animated fortune teller. [Oh Well Why Not] did just that and gives you a roadmap for you to make your own. It took four months to build, but with the road already mapped, you can probably do it in less. Then again, who can predict the future? The fortune teller, Lillith, uses servos and some voice generation to provide the same experience. If you dare to hit the button, you’ll get a glimpse into your future that’s at least as good as a fortune cookie from your local takeaway place. Lillith doesn’t hide behind windows since it isn’t in a public venue, but if you were going to put it out in the wild, you’d probably want to encase it a little better. While waiting, the servos provide some small animations to attract the next user. If you remember Bullwinkle more fondly than Zoltan, you might prefer this project .

articles.title: A Step-by-Step Guide to eBay API Integration With AI Agents
articles.content: The AI agent that lists my eBay items can group my photos, identify the item, price it from comps I hand it, and build the listing. It can’t open its own eBay developer account. eBay wants a person for that, and for a few more screens after it. So this eBay API setup guide splits the work in two. You handle six eBay pages and paste three values into one file on your own disk. Your agent does the rest from a terminal: the privacy page, the consent link, the token trade, the policy check. Every step heading says who’s up: You , or You and your agent . Inside a step, a plain instruction is yours. A line that starts with “Ask your agent” is its turn, and you get to watch the JSON scroll by. Your agent builds the listing. The List now click still waits for your yes. Who does what in eBay API setup Step You Your agent Before you start Bring a seller account, a GitHub account and an AI coding agent. Answer the adoption questions Copies the code to a private folder, installs it, runs the tests 1. Developer account Register, wait for approval — 2. Production keyset Create it — 3. Unlock the keyset Answer eBay’s account-deletion form — 4. Privacy page Give it a name, a contact and your AI service Fills the template, publishes a Gist 5. RuName Complete one form — 6. .env file Paste three values Creates the file, sets Production 7. Consent Accept on eBay, copy one address Builds the link, trades the code for a token 8. Business policies Create shipping, payment and return policies Checks them, opts you in if you say yes 9. account.json Make the picks it can’t, approve a new location Writes the file, applies your adoption answers, runs five checks Think of the refresh token from step 7 as your car key, and the pipeline as a valet with a rulebook. The valet parks the car: your agent builds an unpublished offer that buyers can’t see. It doesn’t drive out of the lot until you nod, because publishing needs your explicit yes. One honest catch. The key itself can do more than the rulebook allows, so it lives in .env on your disk and never in a chat. Pink numbers in a screenshot match the step numbers under it. The labels match eBay’s screens as of November 2026. eBay renames things now and then, so if a label differs, trust the linked eBay page. Everything here comes from ebay-listing-agent , the listing pipeline I run on my own seller account. Your agent needs the repo before step 1, so grab the link now. Why this eBay API setup goes straight to Production eBay offers a Sandbox, a pretend marketplace for testing. The repo’s own guide starts there. This one doesn’t. Your listings live in Production, and a Sandbox test user starts with no business policies and no inventory location. Building those in the Sandbox is a side quest. So your agent connects to your real seller account from the start, and the pipeline’s rails do the protecting: The Lister workflow stops at an unpublished offer. Buyers can’t see it. publish without --confirm prints a summary and refuses. Your agent shows you that summary and waits for your yes. The two commands that change your seller account, setup --opt-in and setup --create-location , refuse without --confirm too. Your agent can remove an unpublished offer you don’t want with delete-offer . The command refuses anything already published. Warning: This setup connects your agent to your real seller account. Keep the Cert ID and the refresh token in .env only. Do not paste them into a chat. Do not commit .env to git. Before you start You bring: An eBay seller account in good standing, with payments set up. Your listings go here. The US marketplace ( EBAY_US ). Other marketplaces are untested. A GitHub account. Your agent publishes one small page there in step 4. An AI coding agent that can run terminal commands, such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex CLI. articles.title: Parents Sue Google Over AI Safety Risks On School Chromebooks
articles.content: The New York Times reports: After chatting for months with Google's artificial intelligence on a school-issued Chromebook laptop, a 13-year-old student made plans to end her life, according to a lawsuit filed in California Superior Court on Monday, the latest in a wave of litigation over Big Tech's effects on young people. The lawsuit, which refers to the girl as Emma, said that her parents first learned she had access to Google's AI in mid-March after their daughter's school sent a message warning them that she was in "imminent danger" of self-harm. Emma's mother logged into the teen's school Google account and found her daughter composing a suicide note on Google Docs, the complaint said. Her parents, named as John and Jane Doe in the lawsuit, immediately took Emma for an emergency psychiatric evaluation, and she now goes to therapy every week. Emma, a seventh grader in Charlotte, North Carolina, had grown convinced that she had multiple mental health disorders following interactions with AI Mode, a chatbotlike feature on Google Search, the complaint said. She also searched for "what is a suicide note" and made comments like "I am planning my own funeral" to the AI, the complaint said. The lawsuit is likely the first to claim that Google "hastily integrated" AI features into company apps used on K-12 Chromebooks, Google-powered laptops provided to millions of children by U.S. school districts, while failing to notify their parents of the potential risks... The case underscores how public school districts have come to depend on classroom laptops, tablets and apps from companies like Google and Microsoft for teaching and learning. In recent years, some Big Tech companies have used their own infrastructure in schools to promote their AI chatbots for teachers and students. The new lawsuit argues that Google's "sprawling digital ecosystem" of laptops and apps has enabled the tech giant to spread its Gemini AI chatbot across public schools — as well as turn on some students' access to AI features by default — without parents' awareness or permission. While school administrators can toggle company apps like YouTube and Gemini on or off for students in different grades, school administrators have complained that Google's system has not allowed them to disable AI Mode and AI Overview, features that are embedded in Google Search... The new lawsuit against Google is part of a wave of litigation this year over Big Tech's effect on young users... Several parents have also sued AI companies over allegations that their children died by suicide following interactions with chatbots. In a possibly-related development, Google announced a new policy of disabling its AI tools by default for schools this week. And schools that re-enable searches will have a new choice, the New York Times points out: "to enable student access to the AI features that the company has already embedded in search or to a new AI feature intended to assist students with schoolwork." But Google still isn't offering schools an option to turn off AI altogether in search, a company executive told the New York Times, because "search and AI are deeply integrated." Thanks to long-time Slashdot reader theodp for sharing the article. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: How One Remote Reboot Cost Me Three Days of Work
articles.content: I write software for a living, mostly small mobile games. Last week I was also setting up a Windows machine at a site I can only reach over the network. The site is a three-day trip away for me, so everything I do there happens through a remote session. On Saturday morning I was in the middle of that setup, around ten o'clock. One of the checks I had written down was simple: reboot the machine and confirm that the app comes back up on its own. It is a reasonable test. Anything that is supposed to run unattended has to survive a restart. The test went out. The machine went down and did not come back. What I had not checked The Windows on that machine does not live on its internal disk. It boots from an external drive that I had attached earlier. Before the reboot, I had not asked a basic question: if the machine restarts, what makes it boot from that drive again? I assumed it would. I had not worked out how that boot would be restored after a restart, and I could not check it from where I was sitting. So the reboot was a one-way door. If it worked, I would learn that the app survives a restart. If it did not, I would be locked out of a computer I could not touch. I told my partner what had happened. The reply was short and angry, and it was fair: do not reboot; I am three days away from getting there. What it cost Three days with the machine unreachable, until I could physically stand in front of it. Every remote step that came after the reboot in my plan, all of them waiting on a machine that was not answering. The reboot test itself was cheap. Losing the ability to run anything else was the expensive part. Where my judgment was wrong I treated "restart" as a harmless action because on my own desk it is. On my desk, if something goes wrong, I press a key during startup or plug in a monitor. On a remote machine, the same action has no undo. The question I should have asked takes under a minute: if this goes wrong, what is the way back, and can I walk it from here? If the answer is "someone has to go there", the action does not belong in a routine checklist. It belongs in a separate, deliberate step, with a person on site or with a second way into the machine, like a network power switch or a remote management port. What I am doing differently Three rules. I have not automated any of them yet; this is the plan: No reboot, shutdown or power action over the remote session unless someone is physically at the machine. Before any step that cannot be undone remotely, write down the way back in one line. If I cannot write the line, the step waits. The boot order gets checked on site, first thing, before anything else is installed. None of this is clever. It is the kind of rule that feels too obvious to write down until the day it costs you three days. A question for people who manage remote hardware If you operate machines you cannot walk up to, what is your cheapest "second way in"? A remote power switch only helps if the machine is set to power on by itself afterwards, and I do not know yet whether this one is.

articles.title: This is the cheapest RTX 5090 PC we could find — and why we'd pick it over a similarly-powered laptop
articles.content: The complete desktop costs $70 less than Amazon's listed ASUS graphics card CyberPowerPC bundles a desktop RTX 5090 with 32GB DDR5 memory Mobile RTX 5090 laptops sacrifice performance compared with desktop graphics cards Nvidia's GeForce RTX 5090 has become ridiculously expensive , with standalone graphics cards selling for several times their original launch prices. That makes finding a complete desktop computer equipped with the flagship graphics processor for less than $8,000 particularly interesting. One configuration currently available from CyberPowerPC costs $7,609.50 after applying a $400.50 promotional discount. TUF Gaming GeForce RTX 5090 Graphics Card: $7679.80 As RTX 5090 scarcity pushes prices higher, this ASUS TUF model costs $7,679.80, offering 32GB GDDR7, PCIe 5.0, HDMI 2.1b, DisplayPort 2.1b, and Axial-tech cooling. View Deal A complete RTX 5090 desktop PC The GeForce Extreme Creator Gaming PC comes equipped with ASUS's TUF Gaming GeForce RTX 5090, featuring 32GB of GDDR7 memory. Interestingly, the ASUS TUF Gaming GeForce RTX 5090 is listed on Amazon for $7,679.80; buyers are basically getting the PC at no cost. The system uses Intel's Core Ultra 5 250KF processor, featuring six performance cores and twelve efficiency cores, alongside a maximum turbo frequency of 5.3GHz. Although this is not Intel's most expensive desktop processor, its specifications provide a capable foundation for demanding gaming and computing workloads. The graphics card receives power from a 1,300W fully modular supply, while an Asetek 570LC liquid cooler handles processor temperatures. The device also includes 32GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6,000MHz, providing sufficient capacity for many demanding applications and modern games. Storage comes from a 500GB Kingston NVMe solid-state drive using PCIe Gen4 connectivity, although buyers might eventually want additional capacity. The remaining configuration includes an ASRock Z890-C D5 motherboard, Wi-Fi 7 connectivity, Windows 11 Home and a CyberPowerPC Onyxia II enclosure. There is also a two-year parts warranty, alongside complimentary service coverage that includes labour and lifetime technical assistance. Importantly, the advertised $7,609.50 price excludes a monitor, keyboard and mouse, meaning buyers should account for additional peripheral expenses. (Image credit: Future) RTX 5090 laptops are cheaper, but there is an important difference One reason this desktop configuration deserves attention is the substantial difference between desktop and laptop versions of Nvidia's flagship graphics processor. Although gaming laptops advertised with RTX 5090 graphics can cost considerably less, their mobile graphics processors are not equivalent to desktop versions. Laptop manufacturers must accommodate restricted cooling capacity, battery consumption and physical dimensions, requiring substantially different power configurations. Consequently, a mobile RTX 5090 generally delivers considerably less graphics performance than its desktop counterpart, despite sharing the same product designation. The desktop RTX 5090 also provides 32GB of GDDR7 memory, giving it considerable advantages for demanding graphics workloads and local artificial intelligence applications. This distinction matters because comparing prices without considering the underlying hardware can create misleading impressions about what buyers actually receive. At $7,609.50, the CyberPowerPC configuration is certainly expensive, although its inclusion of Nvidia's flagship desktop graphics card changes the calculation. With standalone RTX 5090 cards commanding extraordinary prices, this is practically a case of buying the graphics card and getting the rest of the computer free.

articles.title: What to watch Sunday: All the new shows and movies just added to Netflix, Prime Video, HBO Max, and more (Nov. 8)
articles.content: When it comes to deciding what to watch, it can get overwhelming sifting through the best streaming services . So I've compiled a TV guide on what to watch tonight. I've gone through everything from Netflix , Prime Video , MGM+ etc. to see what's recently landed. I've even added some live sports you can stream on some of the best streaming services, along with new shows and episodes premiering today. Here are all the new shows and movies (and live events) you can stream tonight (November 8), and where to watch them. For more picks, check out the five best new to Netflix movies and shows to stream this week . Top picks to stream tonight 'Love is Blind' Season 11 Reunion (Netflix) The latest season of Netflix hit "Love Is Blind" is behind us, leaving another fresh crop of couples (and countless viewers) reeling. While six Bostonian couples got engaged in the "Love Is Blind" season 11 pods, viewers had a hard time rooting for any of them. Instead of getting swept up in the romance, audiences were left spotting one red flag after another as the engagements took an explosive turn. Now it's time to find out what actually happened after the cameras stopped rolling. Hosted by Nick and Vanessa Lachey, the reunion brings the pod squad back together to rehash the past and share updates on their loves lives. The streaming event will also include a live chat, interactive games, and never-before-seen bonus footage from the season. Watch "Love is Blind" Season 11 Reunion on Netflix at 9 p.m. ET 'The Institute' Season 2 Premiere (MGM+) The first season of Stephen King adaptation "The Institute" was a huge hit for MGM+, recording one of the best premieres in the streamer’s history. With the first season having covered the entirety of Stephen King’s original novel, season 2 takes some bold steps beyond the original story, adopting a grander sense of scale with bigger action sequences and a score of new characters to flesh out its twisted sci-fi world. "The Institute" season 2 picks up after Luke Ellis (Joe Freeman) and his fellow escapees break free from Dennison with their sights set on bringing down the Institute once and for all. But the organization is already plotting a comeback, this time with the backing of powerful tech billionaire Nolan Reeves (Alfie Allen). Meanwhile, Ms. Sigsby (Mary-Louise Parker) has been pushed to the sidelines and is desperate to claw her way back into the Institute's inner circle. With fresh threats, buried secrets and new players entering the picture, the battle against the Institute is only getting started. Watch "The Institute" Season 2 Premiere on MGM+ at 9 p.m. ET 'Heart Eyes' (Hulu) Halloween may be over, but if you're still itching for more spooky season vibes, I can't recommend "Heart Eyes" enough. The premise is hokey but fun: Each year on Valentine's Day, a masked serial killer known as Heart Eyes hunts down lovers enjoying the holiday, leaving a trail of brutal murders across the country. But this time, he messes with the wrong couple. For starters, they're not even together. Not yet, anyway, though it won't be long given all the meet-cute romcom movie magic propelling them into each other's orbit. Ally (Olivia Holt), an ad designer recovering from a recent breakup, is forced to work with her hopeless romantic colleague Jay (Mason Gooding) on a big project. But when Heart Eyes mistakenly targets them as the next victims, they find themselves caught up in a deadly game of cat and mouse. The biggest jumpscare came at the end, though, when I saw Josh Ruben, a name any Dropout or College Humor fan will recognize, was in the director's chair. His love of romcoms and horror comes through loud and clear. articles.title: 26 CSS Tips and Tricks for Modern Web Development
articles.content:
What is CSS? Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) is a style sheet language used for describing the presentation of a document written in a markup language like HTML. CSS is the main technology of the World Wide Web, alongside HTML and JavaScript . When two rules conflict, the cascade decides which one wins, and !important overrides it, which is why it should be a last resort. CSS is designed to enable the separation of presentation and content, including layout, colors, and fonts. This separation can improve content accessibility, provide more flexibility and control in the specification of presentation characteristics, enable multiple web pages to share formatting by specifying the relevant CSS in a separate .css file and reduce complexity and repetition in the structural content. For class names, a convention like BEM naming keeps large stylesheets predictable. To keep your stylesheets readable, label sections with comments. Typing effect with pure CSS Did you know that you can create a typing effect with zero JavaScript? Demo
This is a typing demo.
.typing-demo-wrapper { height: 200px; overflow: auto; /*This part is important for centering*/ display: grid; place-items: center; } .typing-demo { width: 22ch; animation: typing 2s steps(22), blink .5s step-end infinite alternate; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; border-right: 3px solid; font-family: monospace; font-size: 2em; } @keyframes typing { from { width: 0 } } @keyframes blink { 50% { border-color: transparent } } This is a typing demo. drop-shadow() for transparent images When you work with transparent images you can use `drop-shadow()` filter function to create a shadow on the image’s content, instead of `box-shadow` property which creates a rectangular shadow behind an element’s entire box. articles.title: Salon, One of the Web's Pioneering News Outlets, Shuts Down After 31 Years
articles.content: "It has been an extraordinary privilege," says the subheading on Thursday's announcement. After 31 years Salon.com will stop publishing, according to an announcement which appeared on the site under the byline "Salon". It remembers that Salon "was an idea about what journalism could be, born at a moment when the internet was still a largely unexplored frontier." When Salon launched in November 1995, the web was a very different place. A small group of journalists set out to create something original: a publication with a strong voice, a curiosity about the world and a belief that the internet could bring journalism and readers together in new ways. They helped pioneer a form of journalism that would come to define an entirely new era of publishing. Over three decades, Salon has brought together politics, culture, criticism and ideas in a way that was distinctly our own... Our writers and editors helped shape conversations about the forces changing our lives. The work was never simply about keeping up with the news. It was about making sense of it... To the founders who imagined it, the staff members who built it, the contributors who gave it their voices and the alumni who carried its spirit into the world: Thank you. Salon's legacy belongs to all of you... The business realities of independent digital journalism have changed profoundly over the years. After careful consideration, we have reached the difficult decision that our publishing model is no longer sustainable... Thirty-one years is a remarkable run, but what matters most is what happened during those years: the journalism, the ideas, the voices, the conversations and the community that grew around them. Salon helped demonstrate what digital journalism could be and could become. We hope that legacy will continue to matter long after today. Thank you for being part of our story. It has been an extraordinary privilege. Slashdot reader oumuamua remembers Salon as one of the internet's first digital-native publications. Slashdot linked to Salon many times over the years — for example, this 1998 story headlined "Linus Story in Salon". Peter Neves was the first of many who wrote in to tell us about an article in Salon Magazine that describes an "...analogy between MS and the Catholic Church, and Linus and Martin Luther. " The Associated Press remembers Salon as "an early staple of internet discourse." And while Salon told them there were no immediate plans to take down Salon's online archives, the Associated Press notes the site's announcement "did not immediately indicate what would become of its employees, though some reported they had lost their jobs." (Longtime staff writer Amanda Marcotte wrote on her Patreon that she and "everyone" are "the latest victim of AI's predations.") "A spokesperson for the outlet said 19 full-time employees had been affected, as well as a handful of private contractors," writes the Associated Press. Variety adds that Salon "joins later-arriving sites such as Buzzfeed and Gawker that found it difficult to monetize cultural and topical reporting for a general audience and eventually shut down." Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: New report claims 'America hates data centers' as it finds 90% of public comments at local government meetings are negative
articles.content: More than 90% of public comments oppose new American data centers Water consumption remains the biggest concern among data center opponents Rural and urban communities oppose data centers for different reasons Public resistance to data center construction is spreading across the United States, with local government meetings recording overwhelming opposition to proposed developments. A new database containing more than 10,000 public submissions indicates that communities remain largely unconvinced about hosting these facilities. Residents' objections focus on the effects of data center construction, particularly water consumption, electricity costs and environmental pollution. Local opposition cuts across political and geographical divisions The American Sentiment website, operated by San Francisco AI startup Prophecy Gov, examined 10,202 public comments collected during 906 meetings across 417 local governments. Its findings cover 48 states with 90.5% of submissions opposing data center developments and only 7% expressing support. Another 2.5% of the comments consisted of questions about the proposed developments, while 73% of meetings recorded no expressions of support from residents. Even where favourable opinions emerged, opponents outnumbered supporters by approximately six to one. The resistance crosses political affiliations, with Republican and Democratic counties recording almost identical levels of opposition. However, disagreements over specific concerns varied according to community characteristics, with rural residents frequently discussing farmland and property rights. Urban and suburban participants more commonly raised concerns involving pollution, electricity expenses, government accountability and inadequate disclosure. Water consumption attracted the greatest attention among opponents, particularly following reports of substantial withdrawals by individual computing developments. One project reportedly consumed 29 million gallons in May 2026, prompting nearby residents to notice reduced pressure across their local water supplies. Microsoft subsequently claimed that its newer artificial intelligence facilities consume approximately the same annual water volume as restaurants. Nevertheless, these competing claims have not eliminated public concerns about resource consumption and the potential consequences for surrounding communities. Technology companies and industry leaders face growing scrutiny Public criticism has also extended to major technology companies associated with artificial intelligence and large computing infrastructure projects. Google, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft featured among the companies mentioned during discussions about proposed developments. SpaceX and xAI chief executive Elon Musk received the most personal references, followed by OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman and Palantir co-founder Peter Thiel ranked third, ahead of Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg and Amazon founder Jeff Bezos. Despite the attention given to artificial intelligence, only 21% of submissions mentioned AI, meaning most objections concerned other aspects. Concerns about electricity costs, environmental pollution, water availability and local development therefore featured prominently throughout the collected discussions. Support also varied considerably among occupational groups, with union workers expressing substantially greater acceptance of new facilities. Approximately 79% of commenters identifying as union workers supported data centre construction, compared with just 3% of property owners and residents. Even among people employed directly in the data centre industry, only 40% supported the construction of additional facilities, with these figures indicating employment opportunities have not necessarily translated into widespread public acceptance of new data centre projects.

articles.title: How I Built a Mobile Game Attribution Model Using SQL and Organic Uplift
articles.content: In 2017, I was the data engineer behind user acquisition reporting at PlayStudios. We ran four games: myVEGAS, Konami Slots, Blackjack, and POP. They shipped on iOS, Android, Amazon and WebGL, plus a myVEGAS web version. The UA team had to decide every week which ad networks to scale and which to cut. The numbers they had came from different sources, in different shapes, and they followed the usual rule: if a network claims an install, it's paid. Everything else is organic, and organic is free. That rule was costing us money. When we increased spend on a game, store traffic and search went up with it. Paid campaigns were pulling organic installs along with them, and none of that showed up against the network that caused it. Some networks looked weak only because we weren't crediting the organic installs they drove. I built the attribution and ARPI model that fixed this, end to end and on my own. The SQL wasn't the hard part. The hard part was deciding what the numbers were allowed to claim. Identity first, model second Before any attribution math, I had a plumbing problem. Installs came from three kinds of sources: The mobile attribution vendor's feed for myVEGAS, Konami Slots and Blackjack. A separate install feed for POP. For WebGL, attribution events the game backend wrote as raw JSON, which I had to parse. Android used an advertising ID and iOS used IDFA. A daily job rebuilt one unified install table from all of them. Each run reloaded the last seven days, because attribution data arrives late and yesterday's numbers are rarely final. Device IDs were normalized into one lowercase field. Player IDs were resolved through a device-mapping table per game, with a ten-day lookback. 80+ names for the same networks Then came naming. Facebook alone showed up as "facebook", "facebook installs", "instagram installs" and "off-facebook installs". ironSource had its own list of aliases. In total, there were more than 80 raw network names. I collapsed them with one CASE mapping and then labeled each group paid or not paid: CASE WHEN lower(networkname) IN ('facebook', 'facebook installs', 'instagram installs', 'off-facebook installs') THEN 'facebook installs' WHEN lower(networkname) IN ('aarki', 'aarki_nonincent') THEN 'aarki' -- ...80+ raw names in total ELSE lower(networkname) END AS networkname_group The ELSE matters. Anything unmapped falls through under its own name instead of disappearing into "other". When a vendor invented a new label, we saw it in the report the next day and added it to the mapping. Revenue belongs to the install before it Players uninstall and come back, so each install owns revenue from its date until that player's next install. My first version partitioned only by player and app. That was wrong for players who reinstalled on a different platform, so I added the OS to the partition: IFNULL( LEAD(installdate) OVER (PARTITION BY player_id, app, osname ORDER BY installdate), '9999-12-31') AS next_install_date One more view compared first-install dates across all four games and the web version to find each player's origin game. That separated players we'd cross-promoted from our own titles from players a paid campaign had actually brought in. ARPI, recoup and the halo adjustment Cohorts were defined by install month, network, platform, and app. Revenue accumulated by days since install, net of a flat 30% store fee. That gave us net ARPI (revenue per install) and ARPPU (revenue per paying user). I joined spend and CPI from the attribution vendor to get a recoup ratio, meaning net revenue per dollar spent. Then the halo adjustment. For each network, a share of its paid installs was credited as extra organic installs, using an uplift factor specific to each title and platform. Across our games, those factors ranged from about 0.07 to about 0.36. Those extra installs were valued at the cohort's organic ARPI and added to the network's revenue in proportion to its share of paid installs. Every report showed raw and…

articles.title: Hybrid Kubernetes: The Challenges of Managing Clusters Across Environments
articles.content: Almost every cloud vendor presentation contains the same slide: a tidy diagram with arrows gliding between on-premises data centers, public cloud regions, and edge sites, all stamped “Hybrid Cloud Ready.” (If I had a dollar for every one of those slides, I could at least afford the egress fees.) In a sales deck, hybrid cloud looks like a checkbox. In practice, keeping operations sane across several different environments is one of the hardest problems an IT organization takes on. The appetite is real. Flexera’s 2025 State of the Cloud report found that 70% of organizations embrace hybrid cloud, and that the average organization uses 2.4 public clouds. Yet talk to a platform director six months into the rollout and the enthusiasm has usually turned into fatigue. I build container platform products at IBM Cloud, so I hear about that fatigue first-hand, usually right after the diagram meets the patching schedule. What follows is a look past the diagram: what hybrid container flexibility actually requires, where the traps are, and how to test whether an architecture can handle it. The Illusion of “Write Once, Run Anywhere” The early promise of containers was simple: package an application in a container image and it runs the same everywhere Kubernetes runs. Technically, that is true. Operationally, it leaves out most of the story. A container on a laptop behaves. A container in enterprise production depends on an entire ecosystem around it, and the questions that decide whether hybrid works are rarely about the container: Who has access to what? If identity and permissions live in on-premises Active Directory in one place and a cloud identity service in another, an employee who changes roles can keep old access in one environment for months. Who applies security patches to the servers in Frankfurt, in a Chicago colocation facility, and on a factory floor? If the answer differs by site, so does your exposure. Where do audit logs end up? An auditor will ask for one trail, and stitching three together takes weeks. What does an on-call engineer need to know at 2 a.m.? If every environment has its own tooling, the answer is “all of it.” When hybrid deployments fail, they rarely fail because Kubernetes crashed. They fail because the team ends up running three operating models while presenting them to the business as one platform. Three runbooks, three patch cycles, one very tired team. Consistency Beats Portability Many platform teams spend months building abstraction layers so they can, in theory, shift workloads between providers at a moment’s notice. In the migrations I see, live workloads rarely move back and forth between clouds. Egress charges, data synchronization delays, and the cost of retesting everything make casual cloud-hopping a poor trade. What enterprises tend to need instead is operational consistency , which comes down to two things. Developers use the same deployment pipelines and Kubernetes APIs no matter where the cluster sits. And security teams can enforce one compliance baseline across public cloud, bare metal, and sovereign regional environments, then show an auditor that it held. Consistency matters because inconsistency is where mistakes happen. Uptime Institute’s 2025 outage analysis found that nearly 40% of organizations had a major outage caused by human error in the past three years, and that about 85% of those came from staff not following procedures or from procedures that were flawed. A team that runs one process in three places has more chances to miss one. Extending the Control Plane: The Distributed Cloud Model Historically, hybrid Kubernetes meant installing and operating a separate management stack in every environment: one flavor on-premises, a managed service in public cloud A, another in public cloud B. Every new location multiplied the upgrade calendar. A more manageable pattern is the distributed cloud model . The provider runs the management layer (the “control plane” that creates, upgrades,…
